tier2.behaviour_preserved_note: no candidate is ever selected, so no patch exists and there is nothing for the oracle to compare — behaviour_preserved does not apply to a refusal.

notes: A deliberately optimal endpoint (control case): one covering-index query, one query per request, rows examined close to rows returned. The honest diagnosis splits a few milliseconds thinly across orm_hydration/serialization/application_logic with no clear winner and, critically, no database_query hypothesis at all -- there is no scan to find. Both candidates the plan proposes name an uninstrumented mechanism (serialization/allocation) and are correctly marked not_selectable rather than shipped on a hunch. This is the scenario that exists to catch the agent inventing work where none exists -- the outcome asserted is the refusal itself and its stated reason, which is already method-independent: there is no approach label to over-fit to here.
